name: Shape M - Extensive Reading (Sustained Silent Reading)
description: Reading lesson built on the research consensus that reading volume is the strongest driver of vocabulary and comprehension growth. Students read self-selected, level-appropriate texts for pleasure with no comprehension testing. Comprehension improves through massive, enjoyable input rather than focused analysis of one text.
pedagogical_justification:
The research consensus (Nation, 2017; Kim & Webb, 2022 meta-analysis, 98 effect sizes) is that volume of reading is the strongest predictor of vocabulary and comprehension growth. Extensive reading is the most divergent from Shape E: instead of one text read intensively, ER uses many texts read extensively, and the form-meaning connection is strengthened through repeated exposure across many contexts rather than teacher-led analysis of a single text.

Five principles drive the design: (1) Students choose what they read — motivation is essential. (2) Texts must be at the right level — 95-98% comprehension without a dictionary. (3) No comprehension testing — reading is its own reward. (4) Volume matters more than depth. (5) The teacher reads too — modelling is powerful, and reading logs, book talks and reading walls make the program visible. ER is a complementary program alongside classroom instruction, not a replacement: it builds vocabulary, speed and habit, while explicit teaching and sub-skill practice belong to other shapes.

This shape is a single ER lesson cycle: SSR (sustained silent reading) → Book talk (sharing, no testing) → Vocabulary spotlight (noticing words from self-selected reading) → Reading log update. Class time here is a 46-minute reading block built around an ongoing ER program.
main_aim_format: By the end of the [program/term], learners will have read [number] books/texts at [level] and developed their reading fluency and vocabulary through sustained silent reading.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, learners will have read for pleasure at their own level and shared one interesting word from their self-selected reading.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
[DD-MM-YY]
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B1
Lesson Shape:
M (Extensive Reading)
Materials:
Classroom library organised by level, reading logs, reading wall, book talk checklist
Assessment:
Reading logs (title, pages, enjoyment rating) — no comprehension checks
Skills:
Reading

stages.stage_aim: To choose a level-appropriate text for pleasure reading
stages.procedure:
- Ss select a book or text from the classroom library organised by level (Oxford, Cambridge or Macmillan graded readers).
- Remind them of the 'right level' rule: they should understand about 95-98% without stopping to look up every word.
- A quick 'five-finger check' on one page helps them judge the difficulty.

stages.stage_aim: To read for pleasure at an appropriate level
stages.procedure:
- Set a 20-minute timer at the start of the reading block.
- Ss read silently. No dictionaries, no stopping. If a word is unknown, read on — the meaning will often become clear.
- The teacher reads too, modelling the habit.
- Teacher circulates quietly, without interrupting.

stages.stage_aim: To share reading experiences and recommend books
stages.procedure:
- In groups of three or four, Ss briefly share what they are reading and why they like it. 3-4 min.
- No comprehension questions — just sharing. 
- Encourage Ss to recommend their book to a classmate who has not tried it. 2 min.
- Teacher listens for engagement and may ask a book talk question to extend thinking.

stages.stage_aim: To notice and learn words from self-selected reading
stages.procedure:
- Ss share 1-2 interesting words they met in their reading today. The teacher writes them on the board.
- Brief whole-class discussion of meaning. Ss say what they think it means and check the context.
- Where possible, note the word family (e.g. decide, decision).

- Ss update their reading logs: title, pages read, enjoyment rating (1-5 stars).
- Ss add today's new words to their personal word list if they wish.
- Teacher reminds Ss of the target for the term and points to the reading wall to celebrate progress.
